entities.summary: Gustav Mahler was an Austro-Bohemian Romantic composer, and one of the leading conductors of his generation. As a composer he acted as a bridge between the 19th-century Austro-German tradition and the modernism of the early 20th century. While in his lifetime his status as a conductor was established beyond question, his own music gained wide popularity only after periods of relative neglect, which included a ban on its performance in much of Europe during the Nazi era. After 1945 his compositions were rediscovered by a new generation of listeners; Mahler then became one of the most frequently performed and recorded of all composers, a position he has sustained into the 21st century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a bridge between 19th-century Austro-German tradition and modernism, Mahler's compositions had significant regional impact, influencing generations of composers and conductors. His music experienced periods of relative neglect during the Nazi era, but post-1945 rediscovery led to widespread popularity, making him one of the most frequently performed and recorded composers.
